items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Councillor Bodaly opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we are gathering from today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishnaabe and Neutral People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share their land today.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Councillor Bodaly provided Council with a moment of reflection.
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.

notes: Formal Public Meeting - DEFFERED

The Formal Public meeting for Zoning By-law Amendment Application Z-23- 09, Canadian Tire Properties Inc., 650, 654, 656, 660 Erb St. W., Ward 2 (Northwest) which was scheduled to occur on Monday, October 2, 2023 has been deferred to October 30, 2023.
For more information regarding the application please contact the planner John Vos at john.vos@waterloo.ca or 519-747-8527.
Formal Public Meeting

items.title: Official Plan Amendment No. 39,
notes: Zoning By-law Amendment Z-22-11,
203-207 King Street South and 10-16
John Street West, 2865161 Ontario Inc.
Report No.: IPPW2023-046
Prepared By: Max Kerrigan
Ward No.: Ward 7 – Uptown
Max Kerrigan gave a presentation outlining the City structure and the major nodes of the City, and detailing the development proposal. He then responded to questions of Council.
Trevor Hawkins, partner, MHBC gave a presentation further detailing the proposed development. He then responded to questions of Council.
Joan Heaton, resident of Waterloo spoke against the proposed development and shared some concerns for the proposed building. They responded to questions of Council.

Richard Magnussen, resident of Waterloo, spoke about how they are pleased to see development, but disapproves the Official Plan Amendment as it is presented. Max Kerrigan responded to questions of Council.
Richard Dixon, Resident of Waterloo spoke against the proposed development, mentioning the zoning by-law. They then responded to questions of Council.
Council meeting recessed: (Time: 7:55 p.m.)
Council meeting reconvened: (Time: 8:01 p.m.)
Ashwin Annamalai, resident of Waterloo spoke in favour of the proposed development, and the community building it would bring.

Carol Dixon, resident of Waterloo raised concerns about the way public notices are provided and spoke against the proposed development. They then responded to questions of Council. Cari Van Niekerk and Max Kerrigan also responded to questions of Council.
Phil Marfisi, resident of Waterloo spoke in favour of the proposed amendments, citing the alignment with the Strategic Priorities.
John Shortreed, resident of Waterloo spoke against the proposed development. They then responded to questions of Council. Max Kerrigan and Joel Cotter responded to questions of Council.
Craig Sloss, resident of Waterloo spoke in favour of the proposed development and about 15-minute cities and the walkability of the City. Cari Van Niekerk responded to questions of Council.
Damian Mikhail, resident of Waterloo spoke in favour of the proposed development, and the sense of community that Waterloo offers.
Shiva Subramanian, resident of Waterloo spoke in favour of the proposed development.
They also suggested that restrictive zoning practices limit what can be built.
Ryan Mounsey, resident of Waterloo spoke in favour of the proposed development, and the need for more housing.
As no one else was present to speak to the application, the Chair concluded the Formal Public Meeting and advised the application is now open to Council for a motion and debate.
Max Kerrigan responded to further questions of Council.

items.title: New Business
notes: Mayor McCabe wanted to thank everyone who came to the Mayor’s Oktoberfest Market organized by the Uptown BIA, staff, and Create Waterloo.
Councillor Roe mentioned the Indigenous Mural unveiling at Wilfrid Laurier on Thursday, September 28th and the importance of representation and reconciliation.
Councillor Freeman mentioned how wonderful Lumen was for the City and wanted to thank staff for all of their hard work on the event.

Councillor Bodaly echoed some of Councillor Freeman’s thoughts on Lumen and its growth over last year. He also spoke about the official opening of Silver Lake at Waterloo Park, and how nicely Lumen tied into it.

Mayor McCabe talked about an event she took part in for Truth and Reconciliation Day as part of her position sitting on the UW Board of Governors. At the Board Retreat they did a Blanket Exercise with the Elder from the University of Waterloo. This experience offered an impactful history lesson on colonization and the residential school system.
